overview: This Senate resolution honors the Blinded Veterans Association on its 80th anniversary. The group was founded in 1945 by World War II veterans who lost their sight in service and is chartered by Congress as the official advocate for blinded veterans. The resolution credits it with helping improve Veterans Affairs (VA) care for blind and low-vision veterans, including rehabilitation centers, guide dog benefits, and adaptive technology, and it notes ongoing needs among rural, aging, and female veterans. It urges the VA to guarantee safe access for guide dogs and their users at its facilities and to have a trained "Service Dog Champion" at each VA medical center. The resolution is not binding and does not change any law or spending; the Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on May 8, 2025.
for: Supporters say the resolution honors eight decades of advocacy that improved care for blinded veterans and spotlights remaining gaps, such as guide dog access at VA facilities.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and changes no law or spending, so its call for guide dog access and a Service Dog Champion at each VA medical center carries no requirement.
